title: people-ops-self-review-manager-prep-scratchpad
content:
Notes to self (rough):

Context: 1:1 with Ethan on Mar 15. Formal mid-year self-review goes live Mar 20. Use this doc to rehearse examples and open questions. Keep it conversational — want to surface concrete signals for promotion discussion and ask for specific stretch opportunities.

Top-line narrative I want to convey:
- Transitioned from IC-level ops execution to partnership/strategy with GTM and Eng in H1.
- Delivered two cross-functional initiatives that reduced recruiter time-to-fill and improved new hire onboarding NPS.
- Growing toward manager-of-managers thinking: coaching peer leads, influencing roadmap for people systems.

Accomplishments (evidence + metrics to cite):
- Hiring funnel improvement: instituted weekly triage with hiring managers + new scorecard => avg time-to-offer down from 42d to 29d (measured Oct 2025 - Feb 2026). Saved estimated ~120 recruiter hours/quarter.
- Onboarding revamp: redesigned week-0 checklist + role-specific playbooks; pilot cohort NPS +0.9 vs previous baseline, ramp time to 80% productivity metric moved from 7 weeks -> 5.5 weeks for product hires.
- Compensation calibration playbook: led calibration for SWE IC bands; created templated docs and training for managers; prevented 6 potential misbands in Q4 cycle.

Behavioral examples for rubric mapping:
- Ownership (example): Took initiative to run cross-team weekly hiring sync after noticing repeated interview no-shows; drove action and created report used by hiring managers.
- Influence (example): Persuaded Eng leadership to adopt structured interview templates by presenting time-saved projections and candidate experience feedback.
- Impact (example): Onboarding changes directly referenced by two hiring managers as reason to expedite offers.

Areas to own next 6 months / Ask list for manager:
- Want lead role on DEI hiring pilot (design cohort sourcing + metricized outcomes). Ask: can I be assigned product-owner for pilot and have 20% allocated time?
- Stretch: mentor one junior people-ops to step into full ownership of intern program ops. Ask: recommend mentee candidate and allow me to run development plan.
- Resource ask: need headcount for 0.5 FTE for onboarding content creation (contractor or internal). Present cost/benefit (estimated 0.5 FTE saves ~200 hours/quarter).

Promotion signals I plan to highlight (put succinctly):
- Scope increased: now managing cross-functional program without direct reports for program execution but coordinating 4 teams.
- Repeatable process: created templates and SOPs used across People Ops vertical.
- Measured outcomes: list of three metrics above with dates.

Potential soft spots / where I want explicit manager feedback:
- Scaling delegation: I still take too many tactical touchpoints on hiring docs; need to shift to coaching. Ask Ethan to give examples where I should have delegated and how to coach.
- Vision articulation: sometimes I lean into execution detail; want feedback on communicating higher-level strategy more often in leadership meetings.

Calibration prep notes (for promotion conversation):
- Competing candidates: baseline expectations for Senior PM of People Ops (not a formal role here) vs Staff-level People Ops. Map my work to Staff-level competencies: cross-functional influence, program ownership, measurable org outcomes.
- Anecdotes to present: two succinct stories (1) hiring funnel win, (2) onboarding pilot success + manager quote. Save quotes in slack copy paste.

Draft self-review bullet points (short):
- Owned cross-functional hiring triage and introduced scorecard that reduced avg time-to-offer by ~30% and saved ~120 recruiter hours/quarter.
- Led onboarding redesign for product org; pilot cohort NPS +0.9 and decreased ramp time to 80% productivity by 1.5 weeks.
- Built a calibration playbook and coached 12 managers during comp cycles, preventing 6 misband decisions.
- Mentored two early-career People Ops partners and started a monthly peer-coaching forum to share hiring best practices.

Manager conversation script (30s elevator + ask):
- Elevator: "Since last cycle I’ve shifted from execution to program ownership across hiring and onboarding — I’ve shipped repeatable playbooks that improved metrics and freed up recruiter time. I want to continue expanding into program leadership (DEI hiring pilot + mentoring) and discuss promotion timing and headcount to scale these efforts."
- Direct ask: "Can we align on 3 signals I need to demonstrate for promotion and a timeline? Also would you sponsor me for the DEI pilot ownership and approve 0.5 FTE for onboarding content?"

Open questions & next steps (actionable):
- Collect manager quotes from slack: search "onboarding takes less" and copy two short lines. (TODO by Mar 13)
- Build short one-pager for DEI pilot with objectives, success metrics, and resourcing ask (first draft Mar 22).
- Ask Ethan for specific promotion rubric owners and whether there is an upcoming calibration meeting I should shadow.
- Practice the elevator and anecdotes out loud twice before 1:1; bring one printed example.

Random scratch ideas to possibly include in package:
- Quick dashboard mock: recruiter hours saved, avg time-to-offer trend, onboarding NPS trend (could attach a sheet later).
- Short video clip of new hire testimonial (5–10s) to include in promotion packet.

Tone reminders: be concrete, focus on impact, avoid apologizing for imperfections, invite explicit feedback and timeline.

End of scratchpad.

(Notes are informal; this file is a private draft for my manager prep and will be cleaned up before any formal submission.)
